chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah has favored Friday over other days, and indeed the gardens of Paradise are adorned and decorated on Friday for whoever attends it. For you compete for Paradise in proportion to your competition for Friday, and indeed the gates of Heaven are opened for the ascent of the servants' deeds.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Friday in Shia Islam regarding Paradise and deeds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the unique ontological status of Friday, describing how Paradise itself is adorned (*tuzakhraf*) for its attendees, linking the physical act of attendance to spiritual elevation. The narration emphasizes a proportional reward system where the haste and eagerness with which believers gather for Friday prayers directly determine their rank in the Hereafter, facilitated by the opening of the heavenly gates to receive their deeds. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Friday as a cosmic axis of divine mercy and spiritual ascent.
